ops.entry: WHEN a criterion keys on a producer's result or payload DO enumerate each field the decision reads by shape, in successful results too, not only per failure cause: null, empty, omitted, wrong type, plus related objects' identity binding. Note what the producer normalizes to a default that must pass.
ops.why: C1 accepted as a sharpening of P-18: my characterization enumerated a producer's outcomes by cause and missed an ok row with a null field that failed open, while the omitted shape is normalized by the producer to a legitimate default that must pass. Old P-18 was scoped to external payloads and container shapes; same length class, broader trigger.

ops.entry: WHEN intent prescribes a literal, verify or printed command DO exercise each against its consumer before signature: verify against the completion state intent predicts, literal through every gate reading it, command pasted verbatim into a fresh shell. Where intent predicts a case still fails, ALL-PASSED is unsatisfiable: split the task.
ops.why: C2 accepted as a generalization of P-08: signed intent dictated an index ruling over its own verify's word cap and printed repair commands that were not runnable as printed (bare script name, punctuation adjoining a path, unquoted). P-08 already covered verify-vs-intent; its task-boundary remedy is kept.

ops.entry: WHEN a plan predicts which checks a change turns red at base DO name each predicted check per assertion, separating cause text from exit and side effect, and gate on predicted set equal to observed set. A prose prediction is unfalsifiable and silently mispredicts rows the census never listed.
ops.why: Own log bullet 4: a prose fail-first prediction was wrong and ungradeable; per-assertion names with predicted_red = observed_red set equality held at validate twice (97=97, 110=110) and made mispredictions loud. Patterns full; displaces P-01, the narrowest pattern (role-identity protection), judged weaker.

ops.entry: WHEN asserting what a mutation or malformed input would do (fail open, crash, misroute) and the case is executable DO run it and cite the measured exit and output before grading severity; a reasoned trace through quoting or exception paths can miss where the code already fails closed.
ops.why: C3 accepted: my goal-check reasoned a swapped-check mutant fails open; QA executed it and measured fail-closed exit 2, and my reasoning was dismissed. O-06/O-07 concern harness validity and free mutants, not executing a severity claim. Outcomes full; displaces O-12, a narrow Python symlink recipe.

originals.original: WHEN a criterion declares what counts as valid or absent in an external payload DO enumerate every field the decision reads, plus the identity binding of related objects, in the criterion and again as per-field graded evidence; container-shape cases alone let each later round surface one more unvalidated field.

WHEN you author a task's verify DO run it against the state the task's own intent predicts at completion, and against the intent prose itself: an ALL-PASSED assertion is unsatisfiable where the intent predicts a case still fails, and the remedy is a task boundary, not verify text.

WHEN a criterion protects objects selected in one role DO grade protection by identity across every role and indirect writer; require overlapping-role counterexamples, not only disjoint fixtures or inspection of the opt-in branch.

WHEN proving a verify block verbatim without touching the file under test DO build a temp root whose data directories are symlinks and whose script is a real COPY: python resolves a symlinked script for sys.path[0], so sibling imports vanish and the run dies in a dependency-missing branch.
